summary: The Castles of Burgundy is a tight, satisfying dice-and-tile-placement euro where you draft hexagonal tiles matched to dice rolls to build out a personal principality across several distinct regions. It rewards efficient planning and flexible dice usage more than luck, making each turn feel like a small optimization puzzle.
praised: elegant, tightly-tuned dice mitigation and tile placement puzzle
strong replayability from varied player boards
clean design with almost no downtime
criticised: can feel a bit dry or solitaire-like with low interaction
phase-based turn structure takes a game or two to click
some find the tile abstraction thematically thin

interaction.kind: mostly parallel play with shared tile market
interaction.detail: Players draft tiles from a shared central display based on dice rolls, so faster or luckier players can snatch tiles others wanted, but most of the game happens on each player's own principality board. There is little direct conflict beyond racing for the same limited tiles.

scoring.why: Points come from filling regions with many different tile types (castles, knowledge, trade, mines, livestock, buildings) plus separate bonus tiles, a hallmark Feld scoring salad.
scoring.how_you_win: You use dice to select and place hexagonal tiles into your princedom's regions, triggering each tile type's own scoring rule plus bonus-tile goals; after five rounds, the player with the most total points wins.
